headline: Low pressure in Bay of Bengal: Signal No 3 issued at four ports
summary: Squally winds of up to 60 kmph are expected in six districts as a low-pressure system forms in the Bay of Bengal.
details: A low-pressure system has formed in the Bay of Bengal, prompting authorities to issue Signal No 3 for four maritime ports.
The weather forecast indicates a risk of squally winds reaching speeds of up to 60 kmph in six coastal districts.
Maritime ports have been warned to keep a close watch on the weather patterns as the system develops.
Residents in the coastal areas are advised to remain cautious as the potential for stormy weather increases.

headline_marked: Historic collapse as [[Bangladesh suffer innings defeat]] in Mackay Test
headline: Historic collapse as Bangladesh suffer innings defeat in Mackay Test
summary: The Tigers were bowled out for under 100 in both innings for the first time in 21 years, ending the series 1-1 against Australia.
details: Australia won the Mackay Test by an innings and 51 runs after bowling Bangladesh out for 95 in their second innings. This result levels the two-match series 1-1 after Bangladesh won the opening Test in Darwin.
The defeat marked a historic batting failure for Bangladesh, as it was the first time in 21 years they have been bowled out for under 100 in both innings of a single Test match.
Mitchell Starc was the standout performer for Australia, claiming 10 wickets in the match, including six in the first innings and four in the second.
Captain Pat Cummins also played a pivotal role, taking six wickets to dismantle the Bangladesh batting lineup.
Bangladesh struggled throughout the second innings, slipping to 39 for three at lunch before collapsing further to 82 for eight.
Litton Das suffered a difficult series, recording a hat-trick of ducks, while skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto was dismissed for 31.
The only bright spots for Bangladesh were Shoriful Islam, who took seven wickets in Australia's first innings, and Mushfiqur Rahim, who fought a lone battle with an unbeaten 29 in the second innings.
caption:
A historic collapse in Mackay! Bangladesh bowled out for under 100 in both innings for the first time in 21 years.

Australia won the Mackay Test by an innings and 51 runs after bowling Bangladesh out for 95 in their second innings. This result levels the two-match series 1-1 after Bangladesh won the opening Test in Darwin.

The defeat marked a historic batting failure for Bangladesh, as it was the first time in 21 years they have been bowled out for under 100 in both innings of a single Test match.

Mitchell Starc was the standout performer for Australia, claiming 10 wickets in the match, including six in the first innings and four in the second.

Captain Pat Cummins also played a pivotal role, taking six wickets to dismantle the Bangladesh batting lineup.

Bangladesh struggled throughout the second innings, slipping to 39 for three at lunch before collapsing further to 82 for eight.

Litton Das suffered a difficult series, recording a hat-trick of ducks, while skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto was dismissed for 31.

The only bright spots for Bangladesh were Shoriful Islam, who took seven wickets in Australia's first innings, and Mushfiqur Rahim, who fought a lone battle with an unbeaten 29 in the second innings.
